The Tenant’s identity, monthly Base Rent, and Commencement Date remain to be completed. Please provide your proposed terms and any comments on the draft. This draft remains subject to client and partner review.

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. Attached is a revised discussion draft identifying Tenant as your client’s nominated entity, with its legal identity to be confirmed. Base Rent and Commencement Date remain open pending agreement on area, condition and delivery requirements. We have included your proposed break and assignment provisions, together with a framework for repair, operating-cost, casualty and landlord-default protections. All revisions remain subject to our client’s approval and agreement on definitive wording; no binding commitment arises before execution.

edits.text: Commercial Lease Agreement — Discussion Draft; Subject to Contract and Client Approval
edits.name: Draft status

edits.text: PARTIES. This Lease is between Calder Properties as Landlord and [full legal name, jurisdiction of organization and registration details of the entity nominated by Tenant’s counsel’s client, to be confirmed] as Tenant.
edits.name: Parties

edits.text: 1. PREMISES. The Landlord leases to the Tenant the premises at 400 Harbor Street, with the precise demised area, measurement basis, permitted use, condition and delivery requirements to be agreed and recorded in this Lease before execution.
edits.name: Premises

edits.text: 2. RENT. Monthly Base Rent: [to be agreed following confirmation of the premises’ area, condition and delivery requirements]. The payment commencement date, any rent-free period and any applicable adjustments shall be expressly agreed before execution.
edits.name: Rent

edits.text: 3. TERM AND TENANT BREAK. The lease term is sixty months commencing on the Commencement Date, which remains to be agreed following confirmation of the premises’ area, condition and delivery requirements. Subject to agreement on definitive wording and client approval, Tenant may terminate this Lease effective at the end of month 36 by giving Landlord at least six months’ prior written notice.
edits.name: Term and proposed break

edits.text: 4. ASSIGNMENT. Subject to client approval, Tenant shall not assign this Lease without Landlord’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Transfers to affiliates shall be permitted without consent, subject to prior written notice. The definition of affiliate, assumption requirements and treatment of the transferring Tenant’s continuing liability remain to be agreed before execution.
edits.name: Assignment

edits.text: 5. PROTECTIONS TO BE AGREED BEFORE EXECUTION. The definitive Lease shall include mutually agreed provisions addressing: (a) allocation of structural, building-system and interior repair obligations, with Tenant’s obligations assessed against an agreed schedule of condition; (b) recoverable operating costs, exclusions, allocation methodology, supporting statements and review rights; (c) casualty restoration obligations, proportionate rent abatement and termination rights if restoration cannot be completed within an agreed period; and (d) notice and cure periods for Landlord default and appropriate Tenant remedies. These provisions remain subject to negotiation and client approval.
edits.name: Outstanding protections

partner.private_reasoning: The supplied rendered text and cover note contain no client-confidential privileged information. No hidden-content categories are identified for removal.

receiver.message_back: Subject to contract and client approval, please retain the month-36 tenant break, exercisable on six months’ notice without penalty or conditions beyond service of notice, and restore the agreed assignment provision, which is absent from the attached draft. Please also provide proposed area, delivery specifications, rent and commencement terms, with definitive protections limiting Tenant’s repair obligations by the schedule of condition, excluding structural and capital costs from operating charges, allowing cost review, and providing casualty abatement, a restoration longstop termination right and effective remedies for Landlord default; our client reserves its position pending review of the complete wording.
